name: The Alps
note: Passes such as the Alpis Graia (Little St Bernard) were deep in snow from late autumn to spring; Ammianus (15.10) describes travellers roped together on the ice.

name: Armenian highlands
note: Xenophon's Ten Thousand lost men to deep snow and frostbite here in the winter of 401–400 BC (Anabasis 4.4–5).

name: Zagros mountains
note: The road up to Ecbatana and the Persian Gates crossed passes over 2,000 m; Alexander forced the snowy Persian Gates in winter 330 BC (Arrian 3.18).

name: Caucasus
note: A wall of mountains crossed only by a few passes such as the Caspian Gates (Darial).

name: Pyrenees
note: The Via Domitia crossed at the low eastern pass (Summum Pyrenaeum), usually open but stormy in winter.

name: Apennines
note: The spine of Italy; the Via Flaminia climbs over it to the Adriatic and the Via Appia crosses it near Beneventum.

name: Dinaric Alps & Pindus
note: Rugged limestone mountains behind the Adriatic coast; the Via Egnatia crosses them by the Candavian range.

name: Haemus (Balkan mountains)
note: The range dividing Thrace from Moesia.

name: Succi pass & Rhodope
note: The Via Militaris crossed the Succi pass between Serdica and Philippopolis, a famous choke point (Ammianus 21.10).

name: Anatolian plateau & Taurus
note: A high plateau with bitter winters; the road south crosses the Taurus at the Cilician Gates.

name: Lebanon & Anti-Lebanon
note: Snow lies on Mount Lebanon for much of the year — the name means "white".

name: Atlas mountains
note: The ranges of Mauretania and the Aurès, home of independent Moorish peoples.

name: Pennines & the Wall country
note: Bleak uplands of northern Britain; the Vindolanda tablets ask for warm socks and underpants.

name: Sahara & Libyan desert
note: Caravans crossed from oasis to oasis, travelling by night in summer.

name: Eastern Desert, Sinai & Negev
note: Roads to the Red Sea ports ran between guarded wells (hydreumata); the Incense Road crossed the Negev.

name: Syrian & Arabian desert
note: Crossed by caravans from Palmyra and by Arab tribes; deadly in high summer.

name: Nile Delta
note: During the inundation the Delta became a sheet of water with towns standing like islands (Herodotus 2.97); people travelled by boat instead of on the roads.
